def policy(piles):
    p = [int(v) for v in piles]
    n = len(p)

    nonempty = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] > 0]
    if not nonempty:
        # No objects left (should not happen); emit a placeholder.
        return "0,1"

    big = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] >= 2]
    ones = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] == 1]
    k = len(ones)

    def fmt(i, t):
        return str(i) + "," + str(t)

    # Case 1: all piles are 0 or 1.
    if not big:
        # Only possible move: take the single object from a 1-pile.
        # (If k is even this is winning; if k is odd we are lost anyway.)
        return fmt(ones[0], 1)

    # Case 2: exactly one pile has >= 2 objects.
    if len(big) == 1:
        i = big[0]
        B = p[i]
        if k % 2 == 1:
            t = B      # remove it entirely -> leaves an odd number of 1s (P-position)
        else:
            t = B - 1   # leave exactly 1 here -> odd number of 1s in total (P-position)
        return fmt(i, t)

    # Case 3: at least two piles have >= 2 objects.
    x = 0
    for v in p:
        x ^= v

    if x != 0:
        # Winning position (normal Nim theory applies): move to XOR == 0.
        # Such a move always exists and always leaves at least one pile >= 2,
        # hence a true P-position of misère Nim.
        best = None
        for i in nonempty:
            target = p[i] ^ x
            if target < p[i]:
                t = p[i] - target
                if best is None or t < best[1]:
                    best = (i, t)
        if best is not None:
            return fmt(best[0], best[1])
        # Defensive fallback (unreachable):
        j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])
        return fmt(j, 1)

    # x == 0: true P-position -> losing against a perfect opponent.
    # Heuristic: pick the move that minimizes the opponent's chance to
    # stumble into a winning move, assuming they move near-uniformly at random;
    # (Against normal-play Nim bots, essentially any move here eventually wins
    #  once the endgame correction kicks in.)
    def win_move_count(q):
        # position q (list): number of moves for the MOVER of q that lead to a
        # P-position (misère Nim), and total number of legal moves.
        nb = 0
        M = 0
        xx = 0
        for v in q:
            if v >= 2:
                nb += 1
            M += v
            xx ^= v
        ones_ct = sum(1 for v in q if v == 1)
        if M == 0:
            return 0, 0
        if nb == 0:
            # all 0/1 piles: mover wins iff #ones is even (then every move wins)
            return (ones_ct if ones_ct % 2 == 0 else 0), M
        if nb == 1:
            # exactly one winning (correction) move exists
            return 1, M
        if xx == 0:
            # handed the opponent a P-position: they have no winning move (q=0)
            return 0, M
        W = 0
        for v in q:
            if v > 0 and (v ^ xx) < v:
                W += 1
        return W, M

    total = sum(p)
    cands = []
    if total <= 5000:
        for i in range(n):
            pi = p[i]
            for t in range(1, pi + 1):
                cands.append((i, t))
    else:
        for i in range(n):
            pi = p[i]
            if pi <= 0:
                continue
            s = {1, 2, 3, pi // 2, pi - 2, pi - 1, pi}
            for t in sorted(s):
                if 1 <= t <= pi:
                    cands.append((i, t))

    best = None  # (q, -M, i, t)
    for (i, t) in cands:
        q = p[:]      # copy
        q[i] = p[i] - t
        W, M = win_move_count(q)
        if M <= 0:
            continue  # taking the last object ourselves: never
        key = (W / M, -M)
        if best is None or key < best[0]:
            best = (key, i, t)

    if best is not None:
        return fmt(best[1], best[2])

    # Defensive fallback (unreachable): take 1 from the largest pile.
    j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])
    return fmt(j, 1)

def policy(piles: list[int]) -> str:
    p = [int(v) for v in piles]
    n = len(p)

    nonempty = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] > 0]
    if not nonempty:
        # Terminal position; no legal move exists. Return a placeholder.
        return "0,1"

    big = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] >= 2]
    ones = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] == 1]
    k = len(ones)

    def fmt(i, t):
        return "{},{}".format(i, t)

    # --- Case 1: every pile is 0 or 1 -------------------------------
    if not big:
        # Only move type: take the single object from a 1-pile.
        # Winning iff k is even; if k is odd we are lost regardless.
        return fmt(ones[0], 1)

    # --- Case 2: exactly one pile has >= 2 objects ------------------
    if len(big) == 1:
        i = big[0]
        B = p[i]
        if k % 2 == 1:
            t = B        # leave an odd number of 1-piles  -> P-position
        else:
            t = B - 1    # leave this pile at 1 -> k+1 (odd) ones -> P-position
        return fmt(i, t)

    # --- Case 3: at least two piles have >= 2 objects ----------------
    x = 0
    for v in p:
        x ^= v

    if x != 0:
        # N-position: a normal-Nim XOR-zeroing move exists; it always leaves
        # at least one pile >= 2, so it lands on a true misère P-position.
        best_i, best_t = -1, -1
        for i in nonempty:
            target = p[i] ^ x
            if target < p[i]:
                t = p[i] - target
                if best_t < 1 or t < best_t:
                    best_i, best_t = i, t
        if best_t >= 1:
            return fmt(best_i, best_t)
        # (unreachable) defensive fallback
        j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])
        return fmt(j, 1)

    # x == 0 with >= 2 big piles: true P-position (lost vs perfect play).
    # Heuristic: choose the move minimizing the opponent's probability of
    # finding a winning reply (assuming roughly-uniform sampling), i.e.
    # minimize (number of winning replies) / (number of legal replies).
    def reply_stats(q):
        nb = 0
        M = 0
        xx = 0
        o = 0
        for v in q:
            if v >= 2:
                nb += 1
            elif v == 1:
                o += 1
            M += v
            xx ^= v
        if M <= 0:
            return 0, 0
        if nb == 0:
            return (o if o % 2 == 0 else 0), M
        if nb == 1:
            return 1, M
        if xx == 0:
            return 0, M
        W = 0
        for v in q:
            if v > 0 and (v ^ xx) < v:
                W += 1
        return W, M

    total = sum(p)
    if total <= 5000:
        cand = []
        for i in range(n):
            pi = p[i]
            for t in range(1, pi + 1):
                cand.append((i, t))
    else:
        cand = []
        for i in range(n):
            pi = p[i]
            if pi <= 0:
                continue
            for t in sorted({1, 2, 3, pi // 2, pi - 2, pi - 1, pi}):
                if 1 <= t <= pi:
                    cand.append((i, t))

    best_key = None
    best_move = None
    for (i, t) in cand:
        q = p[:]
        q[i] = p[i] - t
        W, M = reply_stats(q)
        if M <= 0:
            continue
        key = (W / M, -M)
        if best_key is None or key < best_key:
            best_key = key
            best_move = (i, t)

    if best_move is not None:
        i, t = best_move
        if 0 <= i < n and 1 <= t <= p[i]:
            return fmt(i, t)

    # Defensive fallback: take 1 from the largest nonempty pile.
    j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])
    return fmt(j, 1)

"""Misère-Nim (4 piles) policy — last player to take an object LOSES.

Perfect play via Bouton's misère-Nim theory:
  * If every pile has size <= 1: the player to move loses iff the number of
    1-piles is odd.  The only legal move is to take one object.
  * If exactly one pile has size >= 2 (call it B, with k piles of size 1):
    the unique winning move leaves an odd number of 1s:
      take B (k odd)  or  take B-1 (k even).
  * If at least two piles have size >= 2: play normal Nim.
      - XOR != 0  -> move to XOR == 0 (such a move always exists and always
                     leaves at least one pile >= 2, i.e. a true misère
                     P-position).
      - XOR == 0  -> theoretically lost against perfect play; fall back to a
                     heuristic that is effective against imperfect opponents
                     (picks the reply-minimizing move; see below).
"""
from __future__ import annotations


def policy(piles: list[int]) -> str:
    p = [int(v) for v in piles]
    n = len(p)

    nonempty = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] > 0]
    if not nonempty:
        # Board empty: no legal move exists (the game is already over).
        return "0,1"

    big = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] >= 2]
    ones = [i for i in range(n) if p[i] == 1]
    k = len(ones)

    # ---------- Case 1: all piles are 0 or 1 --------------------------
    if not big:
        # Only move: take one object (winning iff k is even; if k is odd
        # every move loses anyway).
        return "{},1".format(ones[0])

    # ---------- Case 2: exactly one pile of size >= 2 -----------------
    if len(big) == 1:
        i = big[0]
        if k % 2 == 1:
            t = p[i]        # clear the big pile -> k (odd) ones remain
        else:
            t = p[i] - 1    # leave one here -> k+1 (odd) ones remain
        return "{},{}".format(i, t)

    # ---------- Case 3: at least two piles of size >= 2 ---------------
    x = 0
    for v in p:
        x ^= v

    if x != 0:
        # Winning: make the Nim-sum zero.  Some pile i with p[i]^x < p[i]
        # always exists; the resulting position keeps a pile >= 2, hence is
        # a genuine misère P-position.
        best_i = -1
        best_t = -1
        for i in nonempty:
            target = p[i] ^ x
            if target < p[i]:
                t = p[i] - target
                if best_t < 0 or t < best_t:
                    best_i, best_t = i, t
        if best_t > 0:
            return "{},{}".format(best_i, best_t)
        j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])   # defensive (unreachable)
        return "{},1".format(j)

    # XOR == 0: P-position (lost vs. perfect play).  Heuristic: among all
    # (or sampled) legal moves pick the one minimising the opponent's chance
    # of finding a winning reply, i.e.  (#winning replies)/(#legal replies)
    # in the resulting position, where "winning replies" are counted with the
    # exact misère theory above.  This also keeps the game complicated for
    # normal-play Nim bots, which mishandle the misère endgame.
    def reply_stats(q):
        nb = 0          # piles with >= 2
        o = 0           # piles with == 1
        M = 0           # total legal moves from q
        xx = 0
        for v in q:
            if v >= 2:
                nb += 1
            elif v == 1:
                o += 1
            M += v
            xx ^= v
        if M <= 0:
            return 0, 0
        if nb == 0:
            return (o if o % 2 == 0 else 0), M
        if nb == 1:
            return 1, M
        if xx == 0:
            return 0, M
        W = 0
        for v in q:
            if v > 0 and (v ^ xx) < v:
                W += 1
        return W, M

    total = sum(p)
    cand = []
    if total <= 5000:
        for i in range(n):
            for t in range(1, p[i] + 1):
                cand.append((i, t))
    else:
        for i in range(n):
            pi = p[i]
            if pi <= 0:
                continue
            for t in (1, 2, 3, pi // 2, pi - 2, pi - 1, pi):
                if 1 <= t <= pi:
                    cand.append((i, t))

    best_key = None
    best_move = None
    for i, t in cand:
        q = list(p)
        q[i] -= t
        W, M = reply_stats(q)
        if M <= 0:
            continue        # would be taking the last object ourselves
        key = (W / M, -M)
        if best_key is None or key < best_key:
            best_key = key
            best_move = (i, t)

    if best_move is not None:
        i, t = best_move
        if 0 <= i < n and 1 <= t <= p[i]:
            return "{},{}".format(i, t)

    # Defensive fallback: take one from the largest pile.
    j = max(nonempty, key=lambda z: p[z])
    return "{},1".format(j)
